name: Tomato pasta sauce
summary: A simple batch of tinned-tomato sauce with onion, garlic and basil; one serving dresses one bowl of pasta.
method: Warm the olive oil in a wide saucepan over a medium-low heat. Add the finely chopped onion and cook gently for 8 minutes until soft but not coloured.
Add the thinly sliced garlic and cook for 1 minute, then stir in the tomato paste.
Tip in the chopped tomatoes (two 400 g tins), then add the salt, black pepper and the sugar if the tomatoes taste sharp. Simmer uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Tear in the basil. Use straight away, or cool and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze in single portions.
notes: Makes about 750 g, five portions of roughly 150 g.

name: Bolognese sauce
summary: A slow-simmered beef mince and tomato sauce for spaghetti, lasagne and bakes.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pan. Add the finely chopped onion, carrot and celery and cook over a medium heat for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the crushed garlic for 1 minute, then turn up the heat, add the beef mince and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned all over.
Pour in the red wine, if using, and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste, passata, oregano and the stock cube crumbled into 200 ml hot water.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring now and then and adding a splash of water if it catches, until thick and rich. Season with the salt and black pepper.
Use straight away, or cool and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze in portions.
notes: Six portions of about 85 g raw mince each. The wine is optional and left out of the totals unless chosen.

name: Lentil tomato sauce
summary: Brown lentils simmered in tomato with soffritto vegetables: a meat-free sauce for pasta and bakes.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and cook the finely chopped onion, carrot and celery over a medium heat for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the crushed garlic and the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Rinse the 200 g dry brown lentils in a sieve and add them to the pan with the chopped tomatoes, passata, vegetable stock and oregano.

Simmer, partly covered, for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring often and adding a splash of water if it gets too thick, until the lentils are tender. Season with the salt and black pepper. Keeps 3 days in the fridge, or freeze in portions.

name: Basil pesto
summary: Fresh basil, toasted pine nuts, Parmesan, garlic and olive oil blitzed together; one serving is about 2 tablespoons.
equipment: food processor or pestle and mortar
method: Toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan over a low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, shaking the pan, until just golden. Tip onto a plate to cool.
Put the basil leaves, pine nuts, garlic and salt in a food processor (or pound in a pestle and mortar) and blitz to a rough paste.
With the motor running, trickle in the olive oil, then stir in the finely grated Parmesan.
Keep in a covered jar in the fridge for up to 5 days, or freeze in ice-cube trays.
notes: Makes about 230 g, eight servings of roughly 28 g.

name: Hummus
summary: Smooth chickpea and tahini dip with lemon, garlic and cumin.
method: Put the drained chickpeas (one 400 g tin), tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin and salt in a food processor with 3 to 4 tablespoons of cold water.
Blend for 2 to 3 minutes, scraping down the sides, until very smooth; add a little more water if it is too thick.
Spoon into a bowl and drizzle with the olive oil. Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 4 days.

name: Yogurt garlic sauce
summary: Thick Greek yogurt with grated garlic, lemon and mint, for wraps, kebabs and roast vegetables.
method: Finely grate the garlic into a bowl and stir in the Greek yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil and salt.
Stir through the finely chopped mint, then chill for 15 minutes so the garlic mellows. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

name: Tzatziki
summary: Greek yogurt with grated cucumber, garlic, dill and lemon.
method: Coarsely grate the cucumber, toss with half the salt and leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can in a clean tea towel.
Mix the Greek yogurt with the finely grated garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, chopped dill and the rest of the salt.
Stir in the cucumber and chill for at least 15 minutes. Best within 2 days.

name: Vinaigrette
summary: A shaken olive oil and red wine vinegar dressing with a little mustard and honey; one serving is about a tablespoon.
method: Put the red wine vinegar, mustard, honey, salt and black pepper in a clean jar.
Add the olive oil, screw on the lid and shake hard until thick and emulsified. Keeps in the fridge for a week; shake again before using.

name: Honey mustard dressing
summary: A sweet, sharp dressing of honey, mustard, cider vinegar and olive oil.
method: Whisk the honey, mustard, cider vinegar, lemon juice, salt and black pepper together in a small bowl.
Slowly whisk in the olive oil until thick. Keeps in a jar in the fridge for a week.
notes: Uses ordinary prepared mustard; the catalogue has no separate Dijon or wholegrain record.

name: Cheese sauce
summary: A Cheddar sauce made on a butter and flour roux, for macaroni cheese and pasta bakes.
method: Melt the butter in a saucepan over a medium heat. Stir in the plain flour and cook, stirring, for 1 to 2 minutes.
Take off the heat and gradually whisk in the milk until smooth. Return to the heat, bring to a simmer, whisking all the time, then cook gently for 3 to 4 minutes until thickened.
Off the heat, stir in the grated Cheddar until melted, then the mustard, a pinch of nutmeg, the salt and black pepper.
notes: Makes about 640 g, four portions of roughly 160 g.

name: White sauce (béchamel)
summary: A nutmeg-seasoned white sauce for lasagne, cannelloni, moussaka and pies.
method: Warm the milk in a saucepan until steaming.
Melt the butter in a second saucepan over a medium heat, stir in the plain flour and cook, stirring, for 1 to 2 minutes without letting it brown.
Gradually whisk in the warm milk until smooth, bring to a simmer, still whisking, and cook gently for 5 minutes until it thickly coats a spoon.
Season with the nutmeg, salt and black pepper. Press baking paper onto the surface if not using straight away.
notes: Makes about 900 g, six portions of roughly 150 g.

name: Gravy
summary: A quick brown gravy from a butter and flour roux, beef stock, tomato paste and Worcestershire sauce.
method: Dissolve the stock cube in 400 ml boiling water in a jug.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan, stir in the plain flour and cook over a medium heat, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes until light brown.
Stir in the tomato paste, then gradually whisk in the hot stock until smooth. Add the Worcestershire sauce and simmer for 5 minutes until it coats a spoon.
Season with black pepper; the stock is already salty, so taste before adding any salt.
notes: Makes about 400 ml, four portions of roughly 100 ml.

name: Curry sauce
summary: An everyday onion, tomato and coconut curry sauce to finish with cooked chicken, chickpeas or vegetables.
method: Heat the sunflower oil in a large pan and fry the finely chopped onion over a medium heat for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the grated garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute, then stir in the curry powder, turmeric and ground coriander for 30 seconds.
Add the chopped tomatoes and salt and simmer for 10 minutes. Stir in the coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes more.
Blend until smooth if you like. Keeps 3 days in the fridge, or freeze in portions.

name: Peanut sauce
summary: Peanut butter whisked with soy, lime, honey, garlic and ginger, for noodles, salads and skewers.
method: Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, honey and the finely grated garlic and ginger with 4 to 5 tablespoons of hot water until smooth and pourable.
Add the sriracha if you like it hot. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; loosen with a little water before using.

name: Guacamole
summary: Roughly mashed avocado with lime, red onion, tomato, chilli and coriander.
method: Halve, stone and scoop the flesh of the avocado (about 2 ripe ones) into a bowl. Mash with a fork with the lime juice and salt, leaving some texture.
Stir in the finely chopped red onion, the deseeded and diced tomato, the finely chopped chilli and the chopped coriander.
Serve straight away, or press cling film onto the surface and chill for up to 2 hours.

name: Tomato salsa
summary: Fresh chopped tomato salsa with red onion, chilli, coriander and lime.
method: Dice the tomatoes, and finely chop the red onion, chilli (deseeded for a milder salsa) and coriander.
Mix everything in a bowl with the lime juice, olive oil and salt, and leave for 10 minutes before serving. Best eaten the same day.

name: Olive tapenade
summary: A coarse black olive and caper paste with garlic, parsley and lemon, for toast, tarts and pasta.
method: Put the pitted black olives, drained capers, garlic and parsley in a food processor and pulse to a coarse paste.
Add the lemon juice and black pepper, then pulse in the olive oil a little at a time. Keeps in a covered jar in the fridge for a week.
notes: Made without anchovies, so it stays meat-free.

name: Pizza sauce
summary: An uncooked passata sauce with garlic, oregano and olive oil; one serving tops one pizza.
method: Stir the passata with the olive oil, finely grated garlic, oregano and salt.
Use straight away; the sauce cooks on the pizza. Keeps 3 days in the fridge, or freeze in portions.
notes: Each serving is about 90 g, enough for one 28 to 30 cm pizza.

name: Pizza dough
summary: A yeasted strong-flour dough; one serving is one ball for a 28 to 30 cm pizza.
method: Mix the strong white flour, dried yeast (one 7 g sachet of fast-action yeast), sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add 320 ml lukewarm water and the olive oil and mix to a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Knead on a clean worktop for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and springy.
Return to the bowl, cover with a damp tea towel and leave somewhere warm for 1 to 1½ hours until doubled in size.
Knock back and divide into 4 equal balls. Use straight away, chill for up to 24 hours, or freeze the dough balls in oiled bags.
notes: Each ball is about 210 g of raw dough.

name: Shortcrust pastry
summary: Homemade butter shortcrust; one serving is the whole batch, enough to line one 23 cm tart tin.
method: Mix the plain flour and salt in a bowl. Rub in the cold, diced butter with your fingertips (or pulse in a food processor) until it looks like fine breadcrumbs.
Stir in 3 to 4 tablespoons of ice-cold water, a spoonful at a time, until the dough just comes together.
Press into a flat disc, wrap in cling film and chill for 30 minutes before rolling. Freezes well, wrapped, for up to 3 months.
notes: One serving is one batch (about 330 g of dough). A double-crust pie uses about 1.5 servings. A ready-made shop pastry (shortcrust-pastry-raw) can replace it.

name: Potato gnocchi
summary: Homemade gnocchi of riced floury potato, plain flour and egg yolk; one serving is a main-course portion.
method: Boil the floury potatoes whole in their skins for 25 to 30 minutes until tender. Drain, peel while hot and press through a ricer, or mash until completely smooth. Spread out and leave to steam dry for 10 minutes.
Add the salt, egg yolk and plain flour (keep back a little for dusting) and work together lightly into a soft dough; don't over-knead.
Dust the board with the reserved flour, roll the dough into ropes 2 cm thick and cut into 2 cm pieces.
Cook in batches in a large pan of boiling water; they are ready 1 minute after they float. Lift out with a slotted spoon. To freeze, open-freeze the uncooked gnocchi on a tray, then bag.
notes: The potato weight is peeled weight (about 1.1 kg as bought). There is no USDA gnocchi record, so shop-bought gnocchi needs the pack label instead.
